title: Equivariant projective flat preparation of a generic curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme, $g:C\to Y$ a proper dominant morphism with $C$ integral of finite type over $k$ and geometrically integral generic fibre of dimension one, and $E\subset C$ a nowhere dense closed subset. Let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $k,C,Y,g$, preserving $E$. Write $K=k(Y)$ and $F=k(C)$. There are a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $S$, an integral finite-type $k$-scheme $P$, compatible $H$-actions, equivariant H-projective alterations $b:S\to Y$ and $a:P\to C$, and an equivariant H-projective morphism $f:P\to S$ satisfying $ga=bf$. The field extension $K_0=k(S)/K$ is finite purely inseparable. The generic fibre $P_\eta$ is the normalization of $(C\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$; it is smooth and geometrically integral, and its function field is $F\otimes_K K_0$ (a field). The morphism $f$ is flat and finitely presented with geometric fibres of pure dimension one. The schematic closure $M\subset P$ of the reduced inverse image of $E$ on $P_\eta$ is $H$-stable and finite flat finitely presented over $S$, and $M_\eta$ is finite etale over $K_0$. The empty marking is allowed. Schematic closure is defined by the kernel of restriction of functions to the generic subscheme.

Field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target; it does not refer to a group named H. A normal scheme has integrally closed domains as local rings. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes, finite over a dense open of the target. A purely inseparable extension in characteristic p>0 means that every element has some p-power in the smaller field; in characteristic zero it means equality. All group actions below are by scheme or field automorphisms, and are allowed to be nonfaithful.

Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions, fibre products and dimension use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Etale uses [def-weil-etale-morphism].

Normalization, maximal-ideal-adic completion and formal power series use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: de Jong, Families of curves and alterations (1997), §§2.7--2.10, printed pp.603--605: invariant purely inseparable generic normalization, equivariant Chow preparation and simultaneous flattening. The marking flattening is also ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 2, p.160. Local de Jong PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $X=C_\eta$ and $Z=E\times_CX$ as a closed subset. The generic point of $X$ maps to that of $C$, outside $E$, so $Z\ne X$. Apply [lem-sfb-invariant-marked-generic-normalization] to obtain $K_0,N,D$ and their actions, with $k(N)=F\otimes_KK_0$.

source.place: Tags 0BXT (lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal) and 04KT (lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-reduced), combined with the invariant perfect-closure compositum of de Jong, Families of curves and alterations (1997), §2.7 and Lemma 2.8, printed pp.603–604. The combined argument is agent-written; de Jong Lemma 2.8 omits its proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-normalization-projective-spread] to these data. Obtain the finite normal models $S_0,C_0$, and $T\to C_0\to S_0$ with generic fibre $N$ and invariant horizontal marking $L$, whose generic fibre is $D$. The base $S_0$ is normal integral projective, excellent and Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), combined with normalization in finite function-field extensions and de Jong (1997), §§2.9–2.10, pp.604–605. Integral closure localization and the generic normal-curve comparison are expanded in the retained parent proof, Steps 5–7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flatification-horizontal-curve-pair] to $T\to S_0,L$: the curve is H-projective, its generic fibre is smooth integral of dimension one, and $D$ is finite etale. Obtain a blowup $V=\operatorname{Bl}_I S_0$ and flat finitely presented strict transforms $T_V,L_V$, of pure geometric relative dimensions one and zero, with $L_V$ finite.

source.place: Exposé X Theorem 3.4 proof, Step 2, printed p.160; Stacks 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up and 0GSJ

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-invariant-normalized-blowup-domination] to $S_0,I$. It gives a normal integral projective $S$ with equivariant H-projective birational map $S\to S_0$, the same function field $K_0$, and a map $S\to V$.

source.place: Tags 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); morphisms.tex Tags 035S (lemma-nagata-normalization), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective). Combine product-ideal common domination with the invariant Rees algebra and functorial normalization, as in de Jong (1997) §2.10.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-generic-closure-equivariance] to this domination and the flat transforms. The pullbacks $P,M$ have all the asserted flatness, presentation, dimension and finiteness properties, generic fibres $N,D$, and canonical equivariant maps to $T,S$. The scheme $P$ is integral and $M$ is exactly the schematic closure of $D$ in $P$, including the empty case.

source.place: Exposé X, Theorem 3.4, proof Step 2, printed p.160: after flattening the proper transforms equal base changes. Kernel-of-restriction and torsion-free argument as in Stacks divisors.tex, lemma-strict-transform-flat (Tag 080F); morphisms.tex, lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense (Tag 01RE). Equivariance by invariance of the kernels is the agent-written enhancement.

proof.text: Set $b:S\to Y$, $a:P\to C$ and $f:P\to S$ by composition; the square and actions commute. By [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], $P/k$ is projective. The targets $Y,C$ are proper over $k$ by [lem-pc-projective-proper, lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], hence separated. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-source-alteration-criterion] to $b,a$: their source schemes are integral projective, they are dominant, and their function fields are the finite extensions $K_0/K$ and $F\otimes_KK_0/F$. They are the required H-projective alterations. The preceding generic identifications over $C,K_0$ and the closure identity give all remaining clauses, also when the base has dimension zero.

tool_uses.why: Projectivity of Y over k implies properness, used with proper composition to check separated targets for the final alteration criterion.

Simultaneous flattening of the prepared projective curve and its horizontal finite etale generic marking gives the blowup V and flat strict transforms; this is the existing generic flattening tool, not a replacement of the unit route.
Composition of f:P to S and S to Spec(k) makes P projective over k, as required by the projective-source alteration criterion.
Clause (a) composes proper g:C to Y with proper Y to Spec(k), proving that C is a proper, hence separated, target for the alteration criterion.
